title: Editor E8 slice: Vera's cached prefix can be counted in real tokens, by hand
detail:
Split from PROG-E8 on 2026-11-23. The row's last item (4b, second half): a count_tokens reading of the prefix Vera sends on every turn. No migration, no UI change, no dependency, no model call in any test or probe.

PREMISE RE-TESTED FIRST (ADR-1082). On main the token counting endpoint is called in one place, lib/ai/complete.ts accountedMessage, as a per-request budget quote for the whole request. Nothing measured the cached head by itself, so the only figure anyone had was the 2026-09-08 characters-over-four estimate on PROG-E8.

WHAT CHANGED. (1) lib/ai/vera/agent-claude.ts: the tools a turn sends are now picked by one exported pure function, veraTurnTools (member set, plus the Space manager set, plus the operator set), and runVeraClaudeTurn calls it; the selection is the same filter that sat inline, moved, not copied. (2) lib/ai/vera/cached-prefix.ts (pure, sends nothing): veraCachedPrefix builds the cached head from veraTurnTools, buildVeraSystem's stable block and buildRequestPrefix, the same three functions the live loop goes through; VERA_PREFIX_VARIANTS lists the four tool sets a turn can send (tools render first, so each is its own cache entry); veraPrefixCountRequests gives the two count requests (the prefix with a one-word message, and that message alone, on the tier's model from MODELS); veraPrefixReading turns the two counts into tokens, the tier minimum, the margin and cached yes or no, and throws on a reply that is not a count. (3) lib/ai/models.ts CACHE_MIN_TOKENS: the provider's minimum cacheable prefix per tier, beside MODEL_PRICES and with the same rule (it moves when a tier is re-pointed). (4) scripts/vera-prefix-tokens.mjs: the hand-run reading. It loads the shipped modules, goes through getAnthropic (so the gateway is honoured), and prints one line per tool set. --dry prints bytes and a fingerprint with no key and no network. It is in no package.json script and no workflow, and it exits 0 either way: a reading, not a gate.

TESTS. lib/ai/vera/cached-prefix.test.ts: the prefix is byte-identical at two clock times and two random sources, carries no date, time or uuid, is one marked system block after the tools; a mocked live turn (member, Space manager, operator) hands the loop the same tools and the same marked block; the count requests and the reading arithmetic.

NOT DONE, plainly: THE LIVE READING WAS NOT TAKEN. This slice was built without an API key and made no network call. The offline description on 2026-11-23 (node scripts/vera-prefix-tokens.mjs --dry) was 10,946 bytes for the member tool set, 12,731 for a Space manager, 12,385 for an operator and 14,170 for an operator in a Space they run. Bytes are not tokens, but at that size the member prefix may well sit under the default tier's 4,096-token minimum, which would mean it is not cached at all. Someone with a key runs: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... node scripts/vera-prefix-tokens.mjs and records the numbers and the date on PROG-E8. What to do if it reads short (a longer stable block, or a tier whose minimum is lower) is a product and cost call, not part of this row.

Closed 2026-11-23: the hand-run reading exists and its probe passes. The live reading itself was not taken (no key in the build session); it is owed on PROG-E8.

verify.note: Runs the shipped reading (scripts/vera-prefix-tokens.mjs over lib/ai/vera/cached-prefix.ts) against a recorder in place of the SDK client: no network, no key. Fails on main: there is no reading of the cached prefix. Passes when a reading sends two count requests on the tier's configured model, the first carrying the tools a turn sends and one system block with the cache marker that is byte for byte the stable block a real turn gets, the live turn takes its tools from the same function, the prefix is identical at two clock times, the answer is the difference of the two counts against the tier minimum in both directions, a reply that is not a count is refused, and no package.json script or workflow runs it.
